'''Panayiotis Michael Zavos''' ({{langx|el|Παναγιώτης Ζαβός}}), or '''Panos Zavos''' ({{lang|el|Πάνος Ζαβός}}, {{IPA|el|zaˈvos|pron}}), is a [[physiologist]] who was born in [[Cyprus]] and later emigrated to the United States. Zavos has been the subject of controversy for making unsubstantiated claims that he can clone human beings.<ref name=bbc/><ref name=Indep/><ref name=guardian/><ref name=wired/>

==Academic career==
Zavos received a Bachelor of Science in biology-chemistry in 1970, a Master of Science in biology-physiology in 1972, and an Education Specialist in Science (Ed.S.) in 1976 from [[Emporia State University]] in [[Emporia, Kansas]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.emporia.edu/biosci/people/distinguished-alumni.html|title=Distinguished Alumni - Department of Biology - Emporia State University|website=www.emporia.edu|access-date=September 6, 2017|archive-date=September 24, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190924172013/https://www.emporia.edu/biosci/people/distinguished-alumni.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>{{failed verification|date=November 2019}}{{dead link|date=November 2019}} He earned a doctorate in animal physiology in 1978 from the [[University of Minnesota]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 1, 1992 |title=Register of Ph.D. Degrees, 1976 -- 1986 |url=https://conservancy.umn.edu/handle/11299/108495 |access-date=2024-03-12 |website=University of Minnesota Digital Conservancy |hdl=11299/108495}}</ref> He also received an [[Master of Business Administration|MBA]] in 2008.{{Citation needed|date=November 2019}} He received the Distinguished Alumnus Award from Emporia State University<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.emporia.edu/alumni/awards/distinguished-alumni.html|title=Distinguished Alumni - Alumni Relations - Emporia State University|website=www.emporia.edu|access-date=September 6, 2017|archive-date=September 6, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170906225038/https://www.emporia.edu/alumni/awards/distinguished-alumni.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>{{failed verification|date=November 2019}}{{dead link|date=November 2019}}

Zavos is [[Professor emeritus|Professor Emeritus]] in reproductive physiology at the [[University of Kentucky]].{{citation needed|date=November 2019}} He was named as an Honorary Professor by the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], and as a Professor Emeritus by the Venkateshwara Institute of Medicine in [[India]].{{citation needed|date=November 2019}} He has served as a member of the International Advisory Committee of the Middle East Fertility Society.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mefs.org/index.htm|title=Middle East Fertility Society|last=Luc|website=www.mefs.org|access-date=September 6, 2017|archive-date=September 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170907032749/http://www.mefs.org/index.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>{{failed verification|date=November 2019}}{{dead link|date=November 2019}}

== Human Cloning ==
Zavos  have created and implanted cloned human [[embryo]]s.<ref name=bbc>{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/health/3406129.stm|title=Doctor 'implants cloned embryo'|date=May 1, 2018|via=news.bbc.co.uk}}</ref><ref name="Indep">{{cite news |last1=Connor |first1=Steve |title=Fertility expert: 'I can clone a human being' |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/fertility-expert-i-can-clone-a-human-being-1672095.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220524/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/fertility-expert-i-can-clone-a-human-being-1672095.html |archive-date=May 24, 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |accessdate=November 21, 2019 |newspaper=[[The Independent]] |date=April 22, 2009}}</ref> However, Zavos' claims were roundly dismissed after he failed to produce any proof and have been widely condemned by doctors, politicians, and religious and pressure groups.<ref name=wired/>

Professor Hans Evers, chairman of the [[European Society of Human Reproduction and Embryology]], stated: "All the scientific evidence so far indicates that it is completely impossible to clone humans. Anyone claiming that he is going to clone a human does not know what he is talking about. All these guys, including Zavos are doing damage to the profession and goodwill we have built up for many years in the area of fertility treatments."<ref name="Tele101403">{{cite news |author1=David Derbyshire |author2=Roger Highfield |title=Maverick doctor's baby cloning claim rejected as fantasy |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/science/science-news/3313836/Maverick-doctors-baby-cloning-claim-rejected-as-fantasy.html |accessdate=November 22, 2019 |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] |date=October 14, 2003}}</ref>

Professor Robert Winston, [[Emeritus Professor|emeritus professor]] of fertility studies at Imperial College London, said "I do not know of any credible evidence that suggests Dr Zavos can clone a human being. This seems to be yet another one of his claims to get repeated publicity".<ref name=guardian>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/society/2009/apr/22/human-cloning-panayiotis-zavos|title=Maverick's human cloning claims condemned by leading scientists|first1=Sarah|last1=Boseley|date=April 22, 2009|website=The Guardian}}</ref>

[[Arthur Caplan]], a [[bioethicist]] at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] said of Zavos, "I think he is the most dangerous of the current fringe proponents of cloning, because he knows more, stretches the facts, and seems to be wallowing in a mix of publicity and fund-raising that rests on a foundation of hype."<ref name=wired>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/2009/04/cloneclaims/|title=Return of The Doc Who Cried Clone|magazine=WIRED|access-date=November 29, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref>

[[Secretary of State for Health and Social Care|UK Health Secretary]] John Reid condemned Zavos' attempts to create a cloned human baby as a "gross misuse of genetic science".<ref name=bbc/>

Spyros Simitis, the brother of former Greek Prime Minister [[Costas Simitis]], characterized Zavos's claims as "scientific barbarism". He said that if human cloning were to become reality, it would mean the "end of human freedom and evolution". He also referred to the possible use of [[cloning]] by governments for controlling and shaping society according to the government's will.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.christianconcern.com/our-concerns/bioethics/controversial-fertility-doctor-claims-have-implanted-women-cloned-human-embry|title=Controversial fertility doctor claims to have implanted women with cloned human embryos|website=Christian Concern|date=April 23, 2009 |language=en|access-date=November 29, 2018}}</ref>
